speaker: Arne Slot
quote_text:
Arne, just get your initial thoughts on the game,  first of all. A great game of football. Two teams  
that wanted to play, two teams that wanted to  win, had no intentions to do things that people  
normally don't like to see if they watch a game  of football. So no time wasting, no time leaning,  
two teams that were just for almost 100  minutes trying to win a game of football and  
with some brilliant individual moments. So I've  seen a few from us. But the lead up to the 2-2,  
the ball from the goalkeeper to that was that  midfielder that pretended to play the ball to the  
outside and then played his midfielder was a great  moment from them. And then the lead up to the 3-2,  
the way Mitoma bounced that ball behind his  standing leg towards a midfielder that came  
underneath him were, from their perspective, great  moments. And I think there were many of those  
moments during the whole game from both sides. So  joy to watch. Unfortunately, not with the results  
we wanted. First, Premier League start, Federico  Chiesa, sort of #9. Just talk us through your  
thoughts on that and how he thought he did as  well. I think the biggest quality Federico has  
is scoring goals. So the more you get him in and  around the box, the bigger chance it is for him  
to score a goal. And he got a good chance when Mo,  just before Mo had his big chance, Mo assisted to  
Federico. And for him to have a shot, an open shot  from the 18-yard box is for Federico a very good  
chance because he's such a great finisher. But  well defended by Van Hecke who blocked that ball.  
I think he did even more than I could expect from  him because if you haven't played throughout the  
whole season, hardly ever had any start, and then  to play Brighton away, which is a very good team,  
number eight of the league that can bring in  Mitoma 20 minutes before the end, that tells  
you everything about this league. And then for him  to be out for so long and play a game like this is  
more than I could expect from him. And just  one more from me. Did you learn much more  
about some of your players, obviously Elliott  again, back at the side? Saw him slightly a  
little bit deeper as well. Yeah, I wouldn't  say more, but because if you work with them  
for 10 months, it would be a bit strange if  you learn new things after 10 months. But  
for me, I saw a few things that I think I saw  many things that I already knew, and one of them  
is how close the margins have been throughout  our whole season. And now, with us failing to  
score the third, with us not just missing maybe  this 2 or 3% sometimes in our defensive work,  
immediately leads to us losing games of football.  Although I know it's against Chelsea, I know  
it's against Brighton and we didn't lose against  Arsenal, but I know it's against Arsenal. But we  
won this league because we've been so consistent,  we've done so many things right, but we haven't  
won it in a way like City did it for the last  four seasons where they just could close their  
eyes and they were even falling off. So we've been  very close in terms of quality with all the teams  
we've competed with. That's why it's also such a  big compliment that we won this league by such big  
margins because the quality margins are not so  much different between us and some other teams.  
So that's why it's such a big compliment,  especially because we've had our injuries  
throughout the season as well. And yeah, then to  lead by 12 now, I think. 12 is a big compliment to  
our players. Yes. You mentioned the other day on  today about time wasting most games have dropped  
once, but how refreshing is it to see a team like  Brighton mentioning? Yeah, but don't forget us.  
We always do this. And that's why if another team  does this against us, you get to see a great game  
of football like Paris Saint-Germain, like this  one, and I can come up with many others. But I  
also understand that some teams have different  tactics. So it's not something I blame them for,  
but what my main worry is that there's no tactics  or no answer for me towards time wasting and when  
there's a goal kick, the goalkeeper first looks  left, then right, then walks 15 yards the other  
side. And I say, oh, there's a ball over there.  Let me take that one. Yeah, that is, yeah, you  
cannot find tactics to that. And that is what I've  seen, not only in games against us, but I see this  
throughout the league quite a lot. And when I came  here, the first meeting I had with the Premier  
League people, people said, no, no, this game  needs to be intense. We want to have a high-paced  
game. So I'm hoping that the league will find its  answers to these things. A few friends asking,  
was it Alexis injured or was it left at? Alexis  will not play for us this season anymore,  
so he needs rest at this moment of time to recover  completely and to be ready for the start of next  
season, but that will be no problem for him to be  back next season. No, I think he played throughout  
the last part of the season with the Argentinian  mentality that he has, so never gives up no matter  
what he feels, but it's not smart to play a player  that has not a big injury, but has something,  
then to take the risk with him. You touched  on it earlier with the chance from Mo Salah,  
it was his 300th game tonight, like it's going to  be a fitting moment for him. Can I just get your  
thoughts on what's going to be your head when  that ball comes across? Now, the first thought  
that goes through my head when I see a ball  moving towards Mo, I'm like, it's quite a big  
chance this could lead to a goal, because that's  what Mo normally does. But he's been throughout  
this season almost unhuman. Is that the way you  say it? So, but there were moments in the season  
where he was human, so it's not the first time  that he's not scoring for one or two games in a  
row. But the good thing for us is that this hardly  ever happens, and if it happens, you can be sure  
that he will score in the third game or either in  the fourth game again. Congratulations as well.  
Just a quick one on the Szoboszlai's. Oh, he's a  palace. On Szoboszlai's goal, do you think, did he  
mean it? And were you surprised how much space he  had to do that? Now, what I liked a lot is that we  
mostly have a certain routine in our set pieces,  but we try to tell them if you see something else,  
try to execute it, feel free to execute if you  feel there's another opportunity. And I think  
Harvey and Dom felt that it was a 2v1 in that free  kick and they outplayed that and then I definitely  
feel that Dom meant to shoot that ball on target  because he has a great shot and we ask him use it  
more, use it more, use it more because at training  sessions he scores from every angle. But if he's  
playing, then he's always looking, where is  Mo? So, which is also not a bad idea because  
Mo can score a goal as well. But I don't know how  many goals he is now, but it's getting better and  
better for an attacking midfielder of Liverpool  to have these amount of goals. Thank you.
title: Arne Slot post-match press conference | Brighton & Hove Albion 3-2 Liverpool
